text.p: Solid Financial Markets said on Thursday it raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimates and 12-month share price target for Israel's Orbotech Ltd after the company reported strong first-quarter results.
Analyst Shmuel Ben-Eliezer raised his 1997 EPS estimate to $1.95 from $1.83 and to $2.41 in 1998 from $2.31.

"Based on a P/E (price earning) ratio of 15-17 times 1997 estimated earnings, we are increasing our 12-month price target to $29-$33 and maintain our strong buy recommendation," Ben-Eliezer wrote in a report.
Ben-Eliezer said he did not change his revenue estimates calling for $177 million in 1997 and $214 million in 1998 against $148 million in 1996.
"I think they will show increased profitability," Ben-Eliezer told Reuters. This was due to an expected increase in the weight of hardware sales relative to the revenue from services.
"Margins from services are much lower than equipment sales," he said. "Higher returns are also anticipated due to the benefits of economies of scale as sales expand."
Ben-Eliezer estimated gross profit margins in 1997 would rise to 49.4 percent from 47.1 percent last year.
Orbotech controls more than 70 percent of the world market for automated optical inspection systems for the printed circuit board industry.
